findings: Full JavaScript SDK API reference. Both captures list 28 methods in the top-level index and 21 error-code rows, including seven printer codes.

The app obtains a backend ConnectionToken in onFetchConnectionToken. Account switching changes the token handler, clears cached credentials and reconnects after disconnecting any existing reader. Avoid caching the returned reader because its IP can change.

Payment collection consumes a backend PaymentIntent client secret. Processing takes the successfully collected Intent and returns a confirmed Intent or an error. SetupIntent collection requires its backend-generated client secret and allowRedisplay, then confirmation consumes the returned SetupIntent. Refund processing requires successful refund collection. The operations and their outstanding-command cancellations are separate.
substantive_changes: The account registration prerequisite for app discovery now says smart reader where the May capture named the Verifone P400. Record this as a broader documentation statement for JavaScript smart-reader discovery, without inferring newly supported hardware or a runtime change.

November expands the simulator link into inline explanation of the existing built-in test reader for Terminal SDKs and server-driven integrations. Discovery's default, simulated location exception and configuration lifetime/overwrite behavior are retained.

JavaScript-specific documentation link parameters and the PaymentIntent creation destination are navigation changes. Table compression, heading case/spacing, numbered Markdown, escapes and code-fence changes are presentational.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the full 2026-05-01 raw even though its filename ends in 2025. Both captures carry the 2025-10-30 surcharge consent entry (custom message up to 220 characters), 2025-10-06 V660p print preview and 2025-06-02 simulated input and cancellation changes.

Keep the readerBehavior.allowCustomerCancel default false and dated restricted availability, distinct from per-call enable_customer_cancellation on Android-based smart readers. Keep allow_redisplay required on payment collection when setup_future_usage is set and allowRedisplay required on SetupIntent collection.
Retain V660p-only HTMLCanvasElement print scope and preview attribution, simulator-only behavior, and readReusableCard's lack of standard Terminal pricing/liability treatment for online reuse.
conflicts: The mapped summary, Stripe provider index, company page and stripe-terminal concept say 29 methods and 17 error codes. Both dated captures list 28 method links and 21 error-code rows. Remove the counts or describe the exact scope counted.

Both captures put an apparently wide contactless and wallet saving prohibition under the JavaScript readReusableCard section. The save-payment-details concept describes mobile-wallet saving through the separate SetupIntent flow. Preserve the scoped dated warning and separate authority. Do not use the readReusableCard note as a global finding.

Both captures name cancelReadReusableCard() in the method list and detailed section, but the corresponding error-code prose names cancelCollectReusableCard. Keep the method heading as the reference and avoid claiming an alias.
unresolved_questions: Both captures say collectRefundPaymentMethod takes two required parameters, while listing charge_id, amount and currency in the signature and describing currency without an optional marker. The excerpt does not settle currency requiredness. Avoid resolving it by inference.

findings: Add the November evidence and the dated smart-reader registration prerequisite, keeping the prior P400 wording, existing method routes, and applicable qualifications.
conflicts: Correct 29/17 counts or remove them from source and reciprocal labels. Attribute older change history and scope the readReusableCard restriction without generalizing it to SetupIntent saving.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/references/api/js-sdk, source-stripe-terminal-js-sdk-reference describes a JavaScript app fetching a backend ConnectionToken and reacting to reader state. The reader reports connecting, connected or not_connected and not_ready, ready, waiting_for_input or processing for payments. Account switching disconnects any reader, changes token sourcing, clears credentials and reconnects. Both captures describe this sequence, but the registration prerequisite moves from the Verifone P400 on 2026-05-01 to a smart reader on 2026-11-07 (old raw lines 39-119 and new raw lines 40-120). The app supplies a backend PaymentIntent client secret to collect and passes the returned PaymentIntent into processPayment for confirmation; return_url is used only with redirect-based methods and allow_redisplay is required at collection when setup_future_usage is set. SetupIntent collection requires the backend client secret and allowRedisplay, then confirmation consumes the collected SetupIntent (old raw lines 121-280 and new raw lines 122-281). Refund processing follows successful refund-method collection and the reference separately describes display, simulator, collection, cancellation and V660p printing (old raw lines 301-446 and new raw lines 302-446). The existing summary captures those method groups and the changelog themes, but 28 method links and 21 error rows appear in both captures (old raw lines 10-37 and old raw lines 458-478, new raw lines 11-38 and new raw lines 458-478).

The November inline simulator explanation supplies test context for the existing feature; the default, location exception and simulated-only configuration/reset are retained (old raw lines 67-68 and old raw lines 333-366, new raw lines 68-69 and new raw lines 334-366). JS-specific documentation query parameters and the PaymentIntent creation guide link are navigation changes, while table formatting, code fences and number markers are presentational (old raw lines 114-130 and new raw lines 115-131). Keep the separate SetupIntent-saving authority discoverable via stripe-terminal-save-payment-details.
